summary: Bladen County, NC: steel tower erected by the CCC in January 1935 (99 ft 9 in); Forest Lookouts marks it removed; no site description found.

facts.design: 99-foot 9-inch steel tower with a two-room ground cabin
facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts marks the tower Removed
facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

access.note: OpenStreetMap tags the tower access=no; no other source read describes public access

events.note: Erected by the Civilian Conservation Corps; funded through Emergency Conservation Works

evidence.supports: CCC erected a 99-foot 9-inch steel tower with a two-room ground cabin in January 1935, at a cost of $1,531.97
evidence.quote: January 1935: The Civilian Conservation Corps erected a 99-foot 9-inch steel tower with a 2-room ground cabin for a cost of $1,531.97.
The funding for the project was through the Emergency Conservation Works program.

evidence.supports: page credits the details to the sixth biennial report, 1934-36
evidence.quote: Department of Conservation and Development - 6th Biennial Report 1934-36

evidence.supports: 1937 item: state-operated tower supplemented by a 100-foot tower built by the Resettlement Administration
evidence.quote: A state-operated tower near the area has been supplemented by a 100-foot steel tower put by the Resettlement Administration

evidence.supports: 1937 item: project forester developed a trained, well-equipped force for prevention and suppression of fires
evidence.quote: The project forester has developed a well-equipped force of trained men for prevention and suppression of fires
making it possible to spot any fire on the 30,000-acre project immediately

evidence.supports: agency is the North Carolina Division of Forest Resources
evidence.quote: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

evidence.supports: OpenStreetMap node named Jones Lake Lookout Tower

corrections.why: Source gives 99 feet 9 inches, about 30.4 m; 30.2 m matches 99 feet without the 9 inches

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1937 item quoted on the page credits a 100-foot tower to the Resettlement Administration. The 99-foot 9-inch CCC figure is used for this tower; the page does not say the two are the same structure.

notes_for_editor: The 1935 build, its cost and funding rest on one volunteer page that quotes a 1934-36 state report; no independent confirmation found. One search and a fetch of the Jones Lake State Park page found no tower mention. The brief's 30.2 m appears to be 99 feet without the 9 inches; corrected to 30.4 m. The 1937 item may describe another tower. Worth asking the NC Forest Service or Jones Lake State Park. OSM elevation of 23 m matches the brief.
